source_text: VIII. Ἐπεὶ δέ ποτε κατέπαυσε τὴν προσευχήν, μνημονεύσας ἁπάντων καὶ τῶν πώποτε συμβεβληκότων αὐτῷ, μικρῶν τε καὶ μεγάλων, ἐνδόξων τε καὶ ἀδόξων, καὶ πάσης τῆς κατὰ τὴν οἰκουμένην καθολικῆς ἐκκλησίας, τῆς ὥρας ἐλθούσης τοῦ ἐξιέναι, ὄνῳ καθίσαντες αὐτὸν ἤγαγον εἰς τὴν πόλιν, ὄντος σαββάτου μεγάλου. Καὶ ὑπήντα αὐτῷ ὁ εἰρήναρχος Ἡρώδης καὶ ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ Νικήτης, οἳ καὶ μεταθέντες αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὴν καροῦχαν ἔπειθον παρακαθεζόμενοι καὶ λέγοντες· Τί γὰρ κακόν ἐστιν εἰπεῖν· Κύριος Καῖσαρ, καὶ ἐπιθῦσαι, καὶ τὰ τούτοις ἀκόλουθα, καὶ διασῴζεσθαι; Ὁ δὲ τὰ μὲν πρῶτα οὐκ ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτοῖς, ἐπιμενόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἔφη· Οὐ μέλλω ποιεῖν ὃ συμβουλεύετέ μοι. Οἱ δὲ ἀποτυχόντες τοῦ πεῖσαι αὐτὸν δεινὰ ῥήματα ἔλεγον καὶ μετὰ σπουδῆς καθῆρον αὐτόν, ὡς κατιόντα ἀπὸ τῆς καρούχας ἀποσῦραι τὸ ἀντικνήμιον. Καὶ μὴ ἐπιστραφείς, ὡς οὐδὲν πεπονθώς, προθύμως μετὰ σπουδῆς ἐπορεύετο, ἀγόμενος εἰς τὸ στάδιον, θορύβου τοσούτου ὄντος ἐν τῷ σταδίῳ ὡς μηδὲ ἀκουσθῆναί τινα δύνασθαι.
thought_title: Brought into the city and urged to save himself
orientation: Polycarp has finished praying at the house where he waited, and officers are now bringing him into the city toward the stadium and the proconsul.
pass_a_gloss: But when at last he ceased the prayer, having remembered everyone and those who had at any time met with him, both small and great, both honored and without honor, and the whole universal church throughout the inhabited world, the hour having come to go out, having set him on a donkey they led him into the city, it being a great Sabbath. And the police chief Herod met him, and his father Nicetes, who also having moved him onto the carriage kept persuading him while sitting beside him and saying: For what evil is it to say: Caesar is Lord, and to sacrifice, and the things accompanying these, and to be kept safe? But he at first did not answer them, and while they persisted he said: I am not about to do what you advise me. But they, having failed to persuade him, were saying dreadful words and with haste they put him down, so that as he was getting down from the carriage he scraped his shin. And without turning back, as if having suffered nothing, eagerly with haste he went on, being led into the stadium, so great an uproar being in the stadium that no one was able to be heard.

lemmas.gloss: having remembered, having made mention of
having met with, having come together with
shin, front of the lower leg

choices.term: πάσης τῆς κατὰ τὴν οἰκουμένην καθολικῆς ἐκκλησίας
choices.english: whole universal church throughout the inhabited world
choices.why: brief glossary fixes καθολικός as universal in the worldwide sense; keeps οἰκουμένη as inhabited world rather than importing church language
brief glossary fixes this office as police chief as local arresting officer
keeps literal predicate force of the demanded saying, with Caesar as subject complement
literal passive escape sense here, avoiding a religious saved reading the context does not require

pass_b_english: When he at last finished his prayer, he had remembered everyone he had ever met, small and great, honored and obscure, and the whole universal church throughout the inhabited world. Then the hour came for him to leave. They set him on a donkey and led him into the city, and it was a Great Sabbath.

The police chief Herod met him there, with his father Nicetes. They moved him onto their carriage and sat beside him and urged him, saying, "What harm is there in saying, 'Caesar is Lord,' and sacrificing, and doing the rest that goes with it, and so being kept safe?" At first Polycarp gave them no answer. When they kept pressing him, Polycarp says, "I will not do what you are urging on me."

When they failed to persuade him, they turned on him with dreadful words and hastily dragged him down, so that as he got down from the carriage he scraped his shin. Without turning back, as if he had suffered nothing, he pressed eagerly and hastily onward under guard toward the stadium, while the uproar in the stadium was so great that no voice could be heard.
